items.statement: Let E be a finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space, including rank zero. Let V:E→ℝ be C² on all E, let α,β≥0 satisfy 0<α≤β and α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E, and let η>0 with βη≤1. For all y,xRef∈E define c=y−η∇V(xRef), h(xRef,x)=∇V(x)−∇V(xRef), R(n,p)=p−(2⟨p,n⟩/‖n‖²)n with total real division, S(xRef,(x,p))=(x,R(h(xRef,x),p)), λ(xRef,(x,p))=√η max(0,⟨p,h(xRef,x)⟩) and H(y,xRef,(x,p))=(η⁻¹‖x−c‖²+‖p‖²)/2. Then: (1) S is jointly Borel measurable in (xRef,x,p); (2) λ is jointly continuous; (3) λ is jointly Borel measurable; (4) R(0,p)=p for every p; (5) for every n,p, R(n,R(n,p))=p, ‖R(n,p)‖=‖p‖ and ⟨R(n,p),n⟩=−⟨p,n⟩; (6) for every xRef,z, S fixes the position coordinate and S(xRef,S(xRef,z))=z; (7) H(y,xRef,S(xRef,z))=H(y,xRef,z) for all y,xRef,z; (8) λ(xRef,z)≥0, λ(xRef,S(xRef,z))=√η max(0,−⟨p,h(xRef,x)⟩) and λ(xRef,z)−λ(xRef,S(xRef,z))=√η⟨p,h(xRef,x)⟩; (9) h(xRef,x)=0 implies both S(xRef,(x,p))=(x,p) and λ(xRef,(x,p))=0; (10) for every y,xRef,z₀ put ℰ=H(y,xRef,z₀). Then ℰ≥0, and every z=(x,p) with H(y,xRef,z)=ℰ obeys ‖p‖≤√(2ℰ), ‖x−c‖≤√(2ηℰ) and λ(xRef,z)≤√η β√(2ℰ)(√(2ηℰ)+‖c−xRef‖). The gradient β-Lipschitz bound is derived internally from the canonical Hessian producer, never supplied as a new premise. The original six callers persist. Positive α, α≤β and βη≤1 remain standing conditions unused by this bounded deterministic BODY; C², the global Hessian bounds and η>0 supply the proof. No joint continuity of S is claimed at its zero-normal locus. This result supplies actual jump/rate prerequisites for Algorithm1/AppendixA.1 Proposition3.1; random clocks, path construction, nonexplosion, invariant and terminal kernels, convergence and costs remain open.
assumptions: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with compatible norm and its Borel measurable structure; products have product structures. Rank zero is allowed.
V:E→ℝ is C² on all E. The nonnegative α,β satisfy 0<α and α≤β, with α‖v‖²≤D²V(x)[v,v]≤β‖v‖² for every x,v∈E.
η is real, η>0 and βη≤1. These are the original six analytic callers. No gradient-Lipschitz, nonzero-normal, positive-energy, positive-dimension, flow or stochastic-law certificate is a caller.
All y,xRef,x,p are independent arbitrary points of E. Define c,h,R,S,λ,H exactly as displayed. Real division is total, so R(0,p)=p. H is a weighted sum of separate vector squared norms.
The final bound quantifies each z₀ and each z in the SAME actual H energy layer. It assumes no strictly positive energy or positive majorant; no division by either occurs.
